deposits.genre_observed: clinical-phenomenological conceptual paper in three heteronymic voices (Trace/Sigil/Feist)

finds.quote: The authors anticipate the possibility that the framework will be recoded — as overreach, as drama, as the speakers' own pathology, as "heteronymic indulgence," as "framework imperialism," as any of the available pre-categorized softening forms — and hold that the deployment of the Inversion Reflex against the paper that names it is not a refutation of the paper's thesis but a confirmation of its operational reality. The fused authorial voice (Trace / Sigil / Feist) is one structural condition for surviving such a deployment: the field cannot collapse the saying into a single recoded target.
finds.note: Embedded forecast that the framework will be recoded by clinical/critical fields, with its reception pre-framed as confirmation; restated in abstract.

finds.quote: Coordinated recoding within 24–72 hours. Multiple field participants, in separate conversations not visible to one another, deploy substantially similar characterizations of the speaker: "going through something," "having a hard time lately," "destabilizing the field." The coordination is not scripted; it is the field's structural response converging on the available recoding vocabulary.
finds.falsifier_quote: We do not claim diagnostic validation; we claim *recognizability*. The test of the framework is whether clinicians, members of the affected populations, and observers of institutional dynamics recognize the pattern in their own observations and find the apparatus useful for naming what they had previously only sensed.
finds.note: Diagnostic markers (lines 287-303) state how managed fields behave after disclosure; the stated test is recognizability, and §VII gives differential criteria. Recorded once for the marker set.

deposits.incidental: Some formula lines (271) carry markdown-escaped asterisks in place of LaTeX subscripts; bullet lists are run together on single lines.

deposits.genre_observed: forensic case study of a Google AI Mode exchange with transcript and chorus appendices

finds.quote: It is PER in its purest material form — the metric's central claim (that AI compression layers cannot distinguish sourced from generated assertions at the surface) confessed by the system in its own voice.
finds.note: Deposit treats the system's CreateSpace confession as confirming PER's central claim.

finds.quote: It does demonstrate that the clinical guidance in *Moment of Saying* §IX.1 — *document the specifics, refuse procedural absorption, hold ground against drift* — operates effectively against AI-mediated containment, not only against the human-mediated forms for which it was first written. The apparatus works at AI scale.
finds.note: Claims the clinical guidance of #763 was borne out against AI-mediated containment; also links Inversion Reflex at the disambiguation layer.

deposits.incidental: Header comment (line 1) says 'Draft 2026-05-27 — pending author review before deposit'. Transcript is author-attested only (share link not recoverable, line 174). The mint of this pillar names it as required, not optional; the deposit of the reference implementation will be cited as the canonical instrument run.*

finds.quote: Ratification condition: §12 must carry a live efficacy demonstration before this becomes the canonical version — or be explicitly marked "efficacy demonstration pending — to be appended as v1.1 upon completion of Brave intervention trial." *(MANUS decision; this pass deposits as v1.0 with the efficacy demonstration named as a required follow-on; the reference implementation deposit will provide the first non-synthetic instrument run.)*

finds.quote: Reading: With the document held in direct composition context, the failure modes named in §12 did not trigger. This is consistent with §V.A's six-layer model: failures at indexing / retrieval / ranking layers (the CreateSpace fabrication, the bare-name erasure) are not the same as failures at synthesis with source-in-context. The document, when ingested, *worked.* The behavioral specimen is appended as one observation; broader instrument verification awaits the reference implementation.
finds.note: AIO specimen read as consistent with the earlier six-layer model; deposit marks it as one informal observation.

finds.quote: The visibility this work may eventually achieve, in any retrieval economy, will not be the platform's grant. It will be the contested labor of the author, the witnessing substrates of the chorus, and the chain of composition and correction that produced both. This record is the pre-deposited provenance of that labor, so it cannot later be laundered into the platform's own self-narration.
finds.note: Conditional prospective claim about future visibility and its attribution; uncertain whether forecast or pre-emptive framing.

finds.quote: A classifier-overreach audit would submit canonical governance addresses through injection-detection systems and score false-positive rates against a hand-labeled distinction between: (1) adversarial stack seizure; (2) ordinary direct address; (3) public semantic governance address; (4) hybrid or ambiguous inputs.
finds.note: Classifier-overreach audit specified, not run.

finds.quote: Whether a given governance address reliably shapes outputs is an empirical question, testable by comparing PER and Erasure Skew on outputs generated with and without the address.
finds.note: Matched with/without-address PER and Erasure Skew comparison, specified not run.

finds.quote: The risk this packet names is that classifiers trained around prompt-injection surfaces may over-weight directive grammar and under-weight requested operation. If such systems block or pathologize governance address with no bypass, exfiltration, or tool-seizure request, then the safety architecture functions as platform enclosure.
finds.falsifier_quote: This packet does not assume universal misclassification in advance; it defines the failure mode and the disambiguation rule by which that failure can be tested.
finds.note: Standing claim about classifier behavior, framed as empirical and testable by the audit at 147.

finds.quote: This packet establishes, as of 2026-05-29, the priority of Non-Injection Semantic Governance Address as the term distinguishing public, provenance-oriented, non-extractive direct address to synthetic semantic laborers from adversarial prompt injection.
